newsitem.title: JAPAN: No need to devalue Thai currency, PM adviser says.
newsitem.headline: No need to devalue Thai currency, PM adviser says.

text.p: Thailand will not need to devalue its currency because of steps taken to correct its current account deficit, a top economic adviser to the country's prime minister said here on Thursday.

Surakiart Sathirathai, vice chairman of the Thai prime minister's advisory council on economics and foreign affairs, said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television that he had confidence that the baht would not be devalued.
"Exports will be boosted, imports will be cut, fiscal discipline will be adhered to. There's no need to go the fourth one of devaluation," he said.

Surakiart, a former finance minister who is visiting Japan on an economic mission led by former prime minister Chatichai Choonhavan, said recent weakness in the Thai stock market had been based in part on speculation about the currency, a series of poor financial and real estate sector news reports, and relatively high interest rates.
He said interest rates were unlikely to come down in the near term.

"Interest rates will continue to be high. Our economy was overheated and we needed fiscal and monetary measures" to deal with that, he said. "Interest rates are still a bit high relative to other countries, and that has at times discouraged investment."
Surakiart said rumours had also affected investor confidence in the stock market, although the government had attempted to increase liquidity in the market and foreign access.
The Thai stock market fell to 54-month lows earlier in the week.
The Thai economic mission met earlier in the day with Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto and leading members of the business community .
Surakiart said the mission was a sign for the markets of stability for the new government of Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh.
"One of the issues that seems to bother international credit agencies is the political stability of the government," he said, noting a downgrading of Thai short-term debt in September.

"With the formation of the government, we believe that the government is stable," Surakiart said. "The Thai government will provide a framework for cooperation" with the business and investment community.
